In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new drug resistance model, and may lead to the discovery of novel therapeutic targets in ALL
the mechanisms of resistance to anticancer agents, which is of great interest to clinicians and researchers.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the contribution of BCRP in MX resistance in irinotecans selected cells is negligible, and the resistance mechanism to MX is complex.
MX resistance in CPM-K5 cells is not due to BCRP overexpression, although BCRP may be involved in the overall process.
the BCRP transporter is not responsible for the MX resistance of irinotecan-resistant CPT-K5 human leukemia cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CPT-K5 cell line is a model for multifactorial drug resistance, and that MX is a substrate of the BCRP transporter.
BCRP is not the sole determinant of MX resistance in Cpt11-selected human leukemia cells, but may be a contributing factor.
MX resistance in irinotecans selected CPT-K5 ALL cells is multifactorial and is not mediated solely by BCRP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a single inhibitor of drug efflux transporters may not be sufficient to reverse drug resistance.
MX resistance in CFT-11-selected CPT-K5 ALL cells was not reversed with BCRP inhibition or knockdown.
the contribution of drug transporters in conferring multidrug resistance is not always clear, especially in cells with multiple drug resistance mechanisms.
